{{Quote|Visit Mandalore before Mandalore visits you. Take home some souvenirs—a slab of uj cake and a smack in the mouth.|Baltan Carid|<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref>}}
'''''Uj'alayi''''', or '''uj cake''' when translated from the [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']] [[Language/Legends|language]] into [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]], was a traditional [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] dessert. A flat, dense, and sticky [[Cake/Legends|cake]], ''uj'alayi'' was made using crushed [[Nut/Legends|nuts]], dried [[Fruit/Legends|fruits]], and a sweet spiced syrup known as ''[[uj'ayl]]''. A favorite among Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]], the extremely sweet-tasting uj cake was a mainstay dessert at Mandalorian meals and get-togethers.

During [[Gender/Legends|his]] [[Standard year/Legends|years]] spent on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] training [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] as a member of the ''[[Cuy'val Dar]]'', veteran Mandalorian soldier [[Kal Skirata]] had shipments of ''uj'alayi'' brought in by [[Clone template/Legends|clone template]] and [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]]. Skirata shared the uj cake with his [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] [[Clone cadet/Legends|trainees]], and many grew up with a fondness for the dessert. Later, following the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and the [[Declaration of a New Order|rise]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the [[Clan Skirata|Skirata clan]] enjoyed uj cake during several clan dinners at [[Kyrimorut/Legends|their home]] on [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]. A group of [[Mandalorian Supercommando|Mandalorian supercommandos]] aboard a [[Tra'kad-class transport|''Tra'kad''-class]] [[Assault ship/Legends|assault ship]] also partook of an ''uj'alayi'' cake prior to an [[Second Battle of Fondor|assault]] on a [[Turbulent-class Star Destroyer|''Turbulent''-class]] [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] in [[41 ABY]].

==Description==
Uj cake—the [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] [[Language/Legends|language]] rendering of the native [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']] word, ''uj'alayi''—was a unique culinary creation of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] culture. A flat, dense,<ref name="TMPaC" /> amber-[[Color/Legends|colored]] cake, ''uj'alayi'' was sweet to the taste and very filling.<ref name="HC" /> Uj cake was made from a combination of [[Spice/Legends|spices]], dried [[Fruit/Legends|fruits]], crushed and ground nuts, and the scented ''[[uj'ayl]]'' syrup that gave the cake its sticky composition and sweet taste.<ref name="TMPaC" /> The high [[Sugar/Legends|sugar]] content meant even unpreserved uj cake could last for years.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|277|uj cake}}</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|Jango came and went as he pleased, even if we were stranded. You got your supplies of ''tihaar'' and uj cake, didn't you?|Mij Gilamar, speaking to Kal Skirata about their years on Kamino|<ref name="o66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref>}}
Uj cake originated as [[Ration pack/Legends|rations]] for ancient Mandalorian soldiers, who could cook it in a [[Helmet/Legends|helmet]] before preserving for later consumption.<ref name="CSWE" />

As a member of the ''[[Cuy'val Dar]]'', veteran Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] [[Kal Skirata]] spent close to ten [[Standard year/Legends|years]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]],<ref name="TZ">''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]''</ref> located in the [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> training the [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] of the developing [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]]. During this period of [[Time/Legends|time]], Skirata received shipments of uj cake and [[Alcohol/Legends|alcoholic]] ''[[Tihaar/Legends|tihaar]]'' from the [[Army/Legends|army's]] [[Clone template/Legends|clone template]] and [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalorian leader]], [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]].<ref name="o66" /> Skirata shared his cache of ''uj'alayi'' with his [[Commando/Legends|commando]] [[Clone cadet/Legends|trainees]] during their off-duty time on Kamino,<ref name="HC" /> and uj cake was the first meal the Mandalorian training [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeant]] shared with the [[Null-class Advanced Recon Commando|''Null''-class]] [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|ARC troopers]],<ref name="TZ" /> whom he would later [[Gai bal manda|adopt]] as his sons.<ref name="o66" /> Eating uj cake with Skirata was one of the fondest memories [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] commando [[Darman Skirata|RC-1136]]—known informally as Darman—had of his training on Kamino.<ref name="HC" />

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], following the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and the [[Declaration of a New Order|transformation]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] into the new [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the Mandalorian [[Gender/Legends|woman]] [[Parja Bralor]] taught her [[Marriage/Legends|husband]], [[Fi Skirata]], how to make uj cake. The former [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone soldier]] and adopted son of Kal Skirata, Fi had come to live at the [[Clan Skirata|Skirata clan's]] [[Kyrimorut/Legends|home]] on [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] following his desertion from the Republic's Grand Army. A few [[Galactic Standard Calendar|weeks]] after the rise of the Empire, he put his wife's teachings into action, baking an uj cake for his clan mates. A short while later, during an unofficial celebration of the coming of spring in Mandalore's northern regions, the clan put together a small feast that included ''uj'alayi'' among several other snacks.<ref name="ImpCom501st">''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''</ref>

Decades later, amidst a meeting of the Mandalorian clans at the communal [[MandalMotors Hall]] in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], [[Clan Carid|clan]] [[Chief/Legends|chieftain]] [[Baltan Carid]] referenced uj cake as a potential souvenir for hypothetical tourists traveling to Mandalore. That same year, during a [[Clan Beviin|family]] dinner at [[Beviin-Vasur farm|his farm]] outside of Mandalore's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]], [[Medrit Vasur]] served a plate of ''uj'alayi'' for desert.<ref name="Sacrifice" /> Early in the [[41 ABY|following year]], Mandalorian [[Mandalorian Supercommando|forces]] were [[Mercenary/Legends|contracted]] to capture the [[Turbulent-class Star Destroyer|''Turbulent''-class Star Destroyer]], [[Bloodfin (Star Destroyer)|''Bloodfin'']]. Aboard a new [[Tra'kad-class transport|''Tra'kad''-class]] [[Assault ship/Legends|assault ship]] prior to the [[Second Battle of Fondor|attack]], uj cake was enjoyed by the embarked Mandalorians and the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]], who had been spending time on Mandalore in order to learn new techniques to [[Jedi hunter/Legends|combat]] [[Force-sensitive/Legends|users]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], including her recently turned [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] brother, [[Darth Caedus]].<ref name="Revelation">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
''Uj'alayi'' was first introduced to the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe in the [[2004]] tie-in novel to the ''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]'' [[Star Wars video games|video game]], ''[[Republic Commando: Hard Contact]]'' by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]].<ref name="HC" /> It was featured throughout ''Hard Contact''{{'s}} numerous sequel's in Traviss' [[Republic Commando|''Republic'' and ''Imperial Commando'' series]], including [[Republic Commando: Triple Zero|''Triple Zero'']],<ref name="TZ" /> [[Republic Commando: True Colors|''True Colors'']],<ref name="TC">''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]''</ref> [[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel|''Order 66'']],<ref name="o66" /> and ''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''.<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> The ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' article, ''[[The Mandalorians: People and Culture]]'', detailed information on the Mandalorian cake,<ref name="TMPaC" /> and ''uj'alayi'' also appeared in two of Karen Traviss' entries into the multi-author novel series, ''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]'', entitled [[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice|''Sacrifice'']]<ref name="Sacrifice" /> and [[Legacy of the Force: Revelation|''Revelation'']].<ref name="Revelation" />
